musician_growth.input_summary: I am an independent musician with a new EP coming out. I have scattered ideas for TikToks, a half-built email list, a messy Google Drive, and no repeatable way to turn content into fan growth without spending every day online.
musician_growth.diagnosis: The real problem is not content volume. It is the missing operating loop between creative ideas, campaign memory, scheduled execution, and human approval. The stack should turn messy release-week energy into a repeatable fan-growth machine without removing the artist's voice.

workflows.name: Content Idea Intake
workflows.trigger: Artist drops rough captions, voice notes, lyrics, or links into a Notion inbox.
steps: Classify the idea by release phase.
Attach source files from Google Drive.
Mark each asset as draft, approved, or parked.
workflows.human_check: Artist approves the angle in Notion before anything is scheduled.

workflows.name: Release Calendar Builder
workflows.trigger: A Notion item moves to approved.
steps: Convert the idea into a post brief.
Place it in the release calendar.
workflows.human_check: Artist reviews the weekly queue before Zapier pushes posts to Buffer.

workflows.name: Fan Follow-Up Loop
workflows.trigger: A campaign post or email receives meaningful engagement.
steps: Store learning against the campaign record.
workflows.human_check: Artist reviews Gmail drafts before sending.

implementation_steps: Create a Notion database for ideas, assets, approvals, channels, and release phase.
Organize Google Drive folders by release, asset type, and final approval status.
Build a reusable ChatGPT prompt for turning raw ideas into campaign-ready briefs.
Connect Notion approved items to Buffer drafts through Zapier.
Create a Gmail draft workflow for engaged fans and email-list segments.
Run one release week manually, then automate only the steps that stayed stable.
prompts: Turn this raw music-release idea into three short-form content angles. Preserve the artist's voice and label each angle by audience intent.
Given this week's approved posts, build a release-week schedule that balances announcement, story, proof, and fan participation.
Summarize fan replies into useful language for the next email. Draft one warm follow-up without sounding automated.

score_rationales.impact: High impact because a release campaign directly affects audience growth, email capture, and fan engagement.
score_rationales.reliability: Reliable enough because humans approve creative voice before scheduling or sending anything outward.
score_rationales.fit: Strong fit because the work is repeatable, content-heavy, and benefits from structured memory.
score_rationales.complexity: Moderate complexity because it crosses Notion, Drive, Buffer, and Gmail but avoids custom software.
score_rationales.cost: Low cost because the workflow uses common creator tools and lightweight automation.

solo_founder_ops.input_summary: I am a solo founder juggling sales calls, customer follow-ups, product notes, and investor updates. Everything lives in my inbox and memory, so opportunities slip through the cracks when the week gets busy.
solo_founder_ops.diagnosis: The founder needs a lightweight operating system, not a full CRM overhaul. The highest-value move is to centralize commitments, next actions, and weekly narrative updates so follow-through becomes visible and repeatable.

workflows.name: Commitment Capture
workflows.trigger: A meeting ends or an important email thread changes.
steps: Link the source note or email.
Place the action in a weekly operating board.
workflows.human_check: Founder approves extracted commitments before reminders are activated.

workflows.name: Follow-Up Drafting
workflows.trigger: A commitment is due within 24 hours.
steps: Draft a concise update or ask.
workflows.human_check: Founder edits and sends the Gmail draft.

workflows.name: Weekly Investor Narrative
steps: Draft a short update for stakeholders.
workflows.human_check: Founder reviews and trims the narrative before sending.

implementation_steps: Create a Notion operating board with people, commitments, status, due date, and source links.
Define the minimum fields that must be captured after every call or email.
Use Claude or ChatGPT to extract follow-ups from pasted notes and email snippets.
Build a Make scenario that turns approved commitments into calendar reminders and Gmail drafts.
Create a Friday investor-update template that pulls from the operating board.
Review the board every Monday and remove automations that create noise.
prompts: Extract commitments, owners, dates, and open questions from these founder notes. Return only actionable items.
Draft a concise follow-up email based on this last interaction. Keep it specific, warm, and low-friction.
Turn this week's operating board into a short investor update with wins, risks, asks, and next milestones.

score_rationales.impact: High impact because missed follow-ups and unclear commitments directly affect revenue and momentum.
score_rationales.reliability: Reliable enough because the founder approves extracted commitments before reminders or drafts activate.
score_rationales.fit: Strong fit because the problem is information routing, summarization, and repeatable operating cadence.
score_rationales.complexity: Moderate complexity because email, calendar, notes, and stakeholder updates must stay synchronized.
score_rationales.cost: Low cost because the system can run on existing productivity tools and simple automation.

sales_prep.input_summary: Our small sales team needs better prep before discovery calls. Notes are spread across HubSpot, Gmail, and old docs, and reps waste time assembling context instead of asking sharper questions.
sales_prep.diagnosis: The team is losing leverage before calls because account context is fragmented. The stack should produce a pre-call brief that is consistent enough to trust, narrow enough to scan, and tied directly to better discovery questions.

workflows.name: Account Context Assembly
workflows.trigger: A discovery call appears on tomorrow's calendar.
workflows.human_check: Rep confirms the brief is attached to the right account.

workflows.name: Discovery Question Builder
workflows.human_check: Rep approves the final question set before the call.

workflows.name: Post-Call Next Step
workflows.trigger: Call notes are added after the meeting.
workflows.human_check: Rep reviews the Gmail draft and HubSpot update.

implementation_steps: Define a standard pre-call brief format with account facts, context, risks, and questions.
Create an Airtable table that maps accounts to source links and prep status.
Connect Google Calendar events to a Zapier workflow that finds matching HubSpot records.
Use Gemini or ChatGPT to summarize account sources into the brief template.
Send the completed brief and question set to Slack for rep approval.
Track call outcomes for two weeks and adjust the prompt based on rep feedback.
prompts: Create a pre-call brief from this account data. Focus on current context, likely pain, open questions, and risks.
Generate five discovery questions that would produce useful buying-signal evidence for this account.
Summarize these call notes into buying signals, objections, next steps, and a draft follow-up email.

score_rationales.impact: Meaningful impact because better prep can improve discovery quality and follow-up relevance.
score_rationales.reliability: Reliable when constrained to source-linked briefs and rep approval before customer-facing use.
score_rationales.fit: Strong fit because sales prep is repeatable, context-heavy, and benefits from structured synthesis.
score_rationales.complexity: Moderate complexity because account matching across CRM, email, calendar, and docs can be brittle.
score_rationales.cost: Moderate cost because CRM and automation dependencies may already exist but require setup time.

internal_reporting.input_summary: Our internal reporting is slow and inconsistent. Each Friday people paste updates from Slack, spreadsheets, and meetings into a doc, then leadership still asks what changed and what needs attention.
internal_reporting.diagnosis: The reporting process is slow because status collection and executive synthesis are treated as the same task. The stack should separate structured update capture from leadership-ready interpretation.

workflows.name: Structured Update Collection
workflows.trigger: Thursday afternoon reminder posts in Slack.
steps: Ask each owner for progress, blockers, metric changes, and decisions needed.
workflows.human_check: Team leads confirm their captured update before synthesis.

workflows.name: Leadership Brief Synthesis
workflows.trigger: All required updates are received or the deadline passes.
workflows.human_check: Operations owner approves the brief in Slack.

workflows.name: Decision Follow-Through
workflows.trigger: Leadership marks an item as decision needed.
steps: Post the decision ask to Slack.
Carry unresolved items into next week's report.
workflows.human_check: Decision owner confirms the action before it enters the next cycle.

implementation_steps: Define the reporting fields that every team must submit each week.
Create an Airtable base for weekly updates, source links, blockers, and decision requests.
Build an n8n workflow that posts Slack reminders and writes responses to Airtable.
Use Claude to turn structured records into a leadership brief with facts, changes, risks, and asks.
Add Slack approval before the final report is shared.
Run two manual reporting cycles before automating carryover decisions.
prompts: Normalize these weekly updates into progress, blockers, metric changes, decisions needed, and source links.
Compare this week's updates to last week's report and identify only the changes leadership should care about.
Draft a concise leadership report with facts, interpretation, risks, decisions needed, and unresolved carryovers.

score_rationales.impact: Meaningful impact because faster reporting reduces leadership ambiguity and repeated status questions.
score_rationales.reliability: Reliable when updates are structured first and team leads approve before synthesis.
score_rationales.fit: Good fit because reporting needs normalization, comparison, and concise executive interpretation.
score_rationales.complexity: Moderate complexity because multiple teams, missing updates, and carryover decisions add process risk.
score_rationales.cost: Low cost because Slack, Airtable, Drive, and n8n can support the workflow without custom infrastructure.
